## Summary

- Treat live progress as temporary for `/answer`, `/implement`, and `/fix-pr`, using the non-recursive job-scoped `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- Preserve the existing `AGENT_PROGRESS_POLICY` modes: `disabled` means no progress, `report-only` means non-cancellable progress, and `enabled` means cancellable progress.
- For all three routes, post the durable result with resolved GitHub auth first, then verify and delete any temporary progress comment with the workflow token.
- If durable posting fails, preserve response availability by finalizing the temporary progress comment without retaining progress activity; if both paths fail, fail the finalizer.
- Mark deterministic final results and reject those markers both in the entrypoint envelope and `extract-context`, preventing PAT-authored results from becoming implicit follow-ups or authorizing command suggestions.
- Normalize run IDs consistently for progress creation, final-result markers, and cleanup comparison.
- Leave future `none`/`brief`/`full` final progress-overview presentation as separate policy work.

## Verification

- `npm --prefix .agent run test:ci`
- Focused coverage for resolved-auth posting, workflow-token deletion, progress-disabled direct posting, fallback and double-failure paths, current-run cleanup verification, PAT-like sender filtering, command-bearing self-authored comments, and normalized markers

## AI Review Synthesis

<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis -->
<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis-head: 28f930f04c0db4d379444391e89a0385e743f312 -->

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue

PR #507 restores the Sepo App identity for completed `/answer` responses while keeping temporary progress comments on the non-recursive job token. It posts the answer before deleting the verified progress comment and falls back to merging when posting fails. `/implement` and `/fix-pr` behavior remains unchanged. The implementation and tests are sound for App/OIDC authentication, but unconditional reposting introduces a regression for supported PAT deployments.

## Review

The core design is well-scoped and tested, but PAT-authored answers can re-enter Sepo’s routing as trusted user events. Because PAT authentication is a documented runtime path, this requires a bounded in-PR fix before shipping.

| Issue | Severity | Disposition | Description |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| PAT-backed answers can retrigger or authorize Sepo | BLOCKING | FIX_IN_PR | Unconditional `repost` makes PAT-backed answers User-authored events that bypass bot filters. They can allocate implicit-follow-up runs or turn live command suggestions into authorized routes. |
| Normalize the cleanup run-ID comparison | INFO | FOLLOW_UP | The marker contains a normalized run ID while cleanup compares it with the raw expected value. Current wiring always supplies numeric `github.run_id`, so this is not a present defect. |

## Progress

- Head `28f930f` remains current, the hosted check passes, and an independent reviewer reported `npm --prefix .agent run test:ci` passing.
- Repost-before-delete ordering, merge fallback, token separation, and cross-run deletion protection have focused coverage.
- The rubric review passed all seven applicable dimensions, including surgical scope and release-note policy.
- Best-effort deletion may leave a temporary progress comment beside the final answer after an API failure; this is an acceptable documented degradation.
- Posted one non-duplicate [inline comment](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/507#discussion_r3834158065) on the unconditional repost selection.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>PAT-backed answers can retrigger or authorize Sepo</summary>

**Cause:** [The answer workflow selects `repost` for every resolved authentication mode](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/28f930f04c0db4d379444391e89a0385e743f312/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L594), while the resolver also supports PAT and machine-user credentials. PAT-created events can trigger workflows, and these User-authored comments bypass Sepo’s Bot-only entrypoint and sender guards. On `agent`-labeled targets they enter implicit follow-up processing; a live suggested command can instead be parsed as an explicit, trusted request. [GitHub documents the PAT/App versus `GITHUB_TOKEN` trigger distinction](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/trigger-a-workflow#triggering-a-workflow-from-a-workflow).

**Candidate solutions:**

- Select `repost` only for `github_app` and `oidc_broker`; retain `merge` for `pat` and `github_token`.
- Alternatively, add an equivalent fail-closed identity guard.
- Cover the authentication-mode matrix in workflow tests and align the lifecycle documentation.

**Comments:** One reviewer classified this as `WARNING/HUMAN_DECISION` because this repository currently uses App/OIDC; another classified it as `BLOCKING/FIX_IN_PR`. The synthesis adopts the blocking disposition because Sepo explicitly supports PAT-based downstream installations and this PR directly changes their answer behavior.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Normalize the cleanup run-ID comparison</summary>

**Cause:** The progress marker stores `normalizeRunId(runId)`, while cleanup compares the captured value with raw `GITHUB_RUN_ID`. Both are currently the same numeric `github.run_id`, so cleanup remains correct.

**Candidate solutions:**

- Normalize the expected value with the same helper.
- Alternatively, document and test the numeric run-ID invariant.

**Comments:** This is follow-up hardening only and does not affect the verdict or required fix.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step

`FIX_PR`: Apply one bounded auth-mode gate for answer finalization and add matching PAT-mode regression coverage and documentation.

## Final Verdict

`NEEDS_REWORK`

## Action Items

- [ ] FIX_IN_PR: Repost answers only for App/OIDC authentication, preserve merge finalization for PAT/job-token modes, and test and document the auth-mode behavior.

@sepo-agent /answer but the review doesn't make sense? If we just repost the final answer once it's fine? And we can also skip it by filtering out actions?

Yes—the review is technically valid, but its proposed auth-mode restriction is only one solution.

The original problem was dozens of events from repeated progress edits. A single final repost is fine for App/OIDC: it creates at most one skipped workflow run because the sender is a Bot. The edge case is PAT fallback: [PAT comments appear User-authored](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/28f930f04c0db4d379444391e89a0385e743f312/.github/actions/resolve-github-auth/action.yml#L79-L94), so the current [entrypoint filters](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/28f930f04c0db4d379444391e89a0385e743f312/.github/workflows/agent-entrypoint.yml#L54-L123) may treat that final answer as a follow-up—or as a real command if it contains a live command suggestion.

Filtering is a good fix, but filtering only by `github.event.action` is insufficient because both real comments and reposted answers are `created`. A deterministic hidden “Sepo final answer” marker, rejected in both the entrypoint and `extract-context`, would safely preserve one-time reposting for every auth mode. It would still create one skipped Actions record, but allocate no runner or agent; eliminating even that record requires posting with `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

If you want that approach applied, send:

`@sepo-agent /fix-pr keep one-time final-answer reposting, add a deterministic self-authored final-answer marker filter in the entrypoint and extract-context, and cover PAT plus App/OIDC behavior`
